texts.request: The coding agent asked for: "{need}" (the user's latest request: {user_request}). Does the {skill} skill ({description}) serve what it asked for? Answer yes only when it clearly does.
texts.project: The coding session works inside the {skill} project ({workspace}). The {skill} skill: {description}. Does the user's latest request involve work in this project that the skill covers? Answer no only when the request is clearly about something else.
texts.named: The user's latest request mentions {word}. The {skill} skill: {description}. Does the agent need this skill to act on the request?
texts.offered: The coding session works in {workspace}. Does the user's latest request need the {skill} skill ({description}) for the agent to act on it? Answer yes only when the skill clearly helps with this request.
texts.drift: Which offered skill, if any, directly improves the exact action in the agent's recent tool result? Choose none if the approach already works. A skill covering the same topic is not evidence of misuse; successful gh use for GitHub does not call for a browser or browser-harness hand-over. Latest tool action: {action}
texts.drift_notice: Chauffeur: the {skill} skill fits this work better than the current approach.
texts.label: skill {skill}
